visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short, salt-and-pepper hair and spectacles occupies the center of the frame, dressed in a sharp black button-down shirt. He stands against a studio backdrop featuring a massive, slightly transparent ginger cat's head. His hands are active, gesturing emphatically to underscore his points while he holds a small, black electronic clicker in his right hand. The lighting is even and bright, characteristic of a professional recording environment. (2) The screen shifts to a composite view where the speaker remains in the upper section, and a detailed screenshot of a scientific paper from the journal Nature is displayed below. The paper's title, 'Persuading voters using human-artificial intelligence dialogues,' is prominently visible. The man continues to speak with high energy, using his clicker to navigate or highlight specific sections of the digital document shown on the screen. (3) The speaker returns to a full-screen view, performing a dramatic micro-action by placing both hands over his ears and squeezing his eyes shut to mimic a person refusing to listen to opposing views. His facial expressions are highly mobile and expressive, conveying a sense of shock or urgency. The background cat mascot remains a constant visual element, providing a unique branding context to the studio setting. (4) A sequence of statistical data visualizations and scatter plots is superimposed over the video. These charts, labeled with terms like 'Persuasive effect' and 'Prompt,' use various colors to distinguish between different experimental groups. The speaker appears in a smaller inset window, continuing his narration while pointing towards the data points on the graphs, guiding the viewer's attention through the complex findings. (5) The video concludes with the man leaning slightly towards the camera, maintaining direct eye contact and delivering his final summary points. He uses a pen at one point to emphasize a specific detail on an overlay. The visual rhythm remains rapid due to frequent cuts and textual highlights appearing at the bottom of the frame as traditional Chinese subtitles.

(5) [Subtitle]: 而且是地動山搖. (6) [Subtitle]: 來自MIT、康乃爾大學與牛津大學的團隊. (7) [Subtitle]: 在《Nature》跟《Science》上同步發表研究. (8) [Subtitle]: 他們在2024年美國大選. (9) [Subtitle]: 以及2025年的加拿大和波蘭大選期間. (10) [Subtitle]: 找來數萬名選民跟AI聊天. (11) [Subtitle]: 規模之巨大，簡直是社會科學界的曼哈頓計畫. (12) [Subtitle]: 為什麼搞那麼大? 我們知道談到政治許多人就是. (13) [Subtitle]: 「我不聽 我不聽」 立場不合的證據通通當作沒看到. (14) [Subtitle]: 這讓傳統政治廣告的效果廢到笑. (15) [Subtitle]: 通常只能改變不到1%的選民. (16) [Subtitle]: 但現在AI那麼厲害. (17) [Subtitle]: 不免讓人擔心，AI會偷我們個資、抓我們弱點. (18) [Subtitle]: 來個「精準個人化洗腦」. (19) [Subtitle]: 不過這兩篇研究卻發現，AI根本不需要用上詐騙手段. (20) [Subtitle]: 只要一直「碎碎念」就贏了. (21) [Subtitle]: 這怎麼回事? (22) [Subtitle]: 他們在線上群眾外包平台，招募超過七萬六千名受試者. (23) [Subtitle]: 進入這個圖靈測試. (24) [Subtitle]: 科學家先把受試者對於某個議題. (25) [Subtitle]: 比如支持川普或反對迷幻藥的立場. (26) [Subtitle]: 量化成0到100分. (27) [Subtitle]: 接著丟進一個聊天室，跟GPT-4等級的AI開始尬聊. (28) [Subtitle]: 重點來了，科學家已經給AI植入不同的. (29) [Subtitle]: 「說服戰術模組」. (30) [Subtitle]: A組切個資，針對受試者的年齡、性別、種族量身打造話術. (31) [Subtitle]: B組玩情感，用感性故事和道德框架來軟化對方. (32) [Subtitle]: C組則用海量的「客觀事實和證據」轟炸. (33) [Subtitle]: 另外再加上完全聊無關主題的對照組. (34) [Subtitle]: 以及無特殊戰術指示，純自由發揮的基本指令組. (35) [Subtitle]: 數萬場辯論後，科學家再測量立場分數的變化. (36) [Subtitle]: 結果原本大家以為最可怕的「A組個資」戰術，效果只有一點點點點. (37) [Subtitle]: 真正的強者是「C組」. (38) [Subtitle]: 當AI開啟「資料轟炸模式」，說服力比起基本指令組高出了27%啊! (39) [Subtitle]: 好，既然知道「資料轟炸」是最強策略，那就來看效果囉. (40) [Subtitle]: 他們把這套AI拿去挑戰2024年美國總統大選. (41) [Subtitle]: 發現處理川普對決賀錦麗這個極端戰場上. (42) [Subtitle]: AI成功讓川普支持者對賀錦麗的好感度增加了3.9分. (43) [Subtitle]: 賀錦麗支持者對川普則增加了2.3分. (44) [Subtitle]: 不要小看這幾分，在一個五五波的選舉裡. (49) [Subtitle]: 加上個人化設定和額外的AI訓練. (50) [Subtitle]: 針對原本持反對意見的人，AI可以讓他們的態度轉變達到驚人的26.1分. (51) [Subtitle]: 科學家說這已經是民主破壞等級了. (52) [Subtitle]: 簡單來說，科學家證實要改變一個人的政治信仰不需要讀心.
